questions.prompt: The clear corridor is blocked, while a screenshot looks attractive. What is established?

options.label: Appearance does not establish a traversable collision route.
A trigger policy removes every obstacle.

questions.explanation: Traversal depends on the stated collision layout and player footprint. Appearance and trigger logic are independent; neither attractive textures nor an event policy supplies a missing route.

questions.prompt: An overlap handler does not fire. Which independent condition belongs in the review?

options.label: Only the event graph’s label matters.
Every visually intersecting mesh must always emit the event.
Check overlap-event configuration on both participating collision components.

questions.explanation: The cited event contract includes the applicable overlap settings on both sides. Visual intersection alone and a graph label do not establish a configured collision event.

questions.prompt: A visitor enters the exit volume before the player. Under the declared policy, what happens?

options.label: The visitor receives the player’s identity automatically.
The exit remains closed; filter the actor before activation.

questions.explanation: The authored interaction accepts only the declared player identity. An overlap is input to the filter, not authority to activate or to transform another actor into the player.

questions.prompt: Visitor-enter, player-enter, player-enter, player-exit occur in one session. What is the result?

options.label: The exit is open with one activation.
The exit closes on player-exit regardless of policy.

questions.explanation: The idempotent state rule accepts the first allowed enter and keeps later events from awarding again. No close-on-exit rule was declared; visitor input remains rejected.

questions.prompt: A delayed event from an old level arrives after reset. Under the exercise’s rule, what follows?

options.label: Always apply it to the new level.
A reset changes only textures and never state.
Reject the old-session event; the reset state belongs to the new session.

questions.explanation: Session identity protects the reset transition from delayed old work. Applying stale events would violate the declared new closed state; texture changes do not define this lifecycle boundary.
